title: Fukuoka
intro: This trip explicitly skips Tokyo/Akihabara and Osaka/Den Den Town, so here's the regional answer instead — set expectations as "solid regional branch," not Tokyo/Osaka flagship depth on any one hot category (Pokémon cards, current-season figures) specifically.

items.name: Animate Fukuoka PARCO
items.why: A real, non-token branch of the national anime-goods chain.

items.name: Mandarake Fukuoka
items.why: Two floors of games/toys/cards/vintage on 1F and cosplay/dolls/doujinshi on 2F, duty-free over ¥5,000.

items.name: Gashapon Department Store
items.why: Opened 2020, ~2,200 capsule-toy machines — Fukuoka's dedicated gacha landmark.

items.name: Culture Arts
items.how: 3rd floor of an apartment building near Tenjin.
items.why: An independent retro-game shop that comes up repeatedly as the locals'/enthusiasts' non-chain alternative.

items.name: Taito Station Fukuoka Tenjin
items.why: Anchors a reported cluster with nearby GiGO and Round1 locations.
items.crowd_tip: The cluster is unconfirmed beyond blog mentions — worth a look on the ground.

title: Sapporo
intro: Tanukikoji itself is worth a browse beyond C-pla — the city's own tourism board confirms game centers and anime-goods shops scattered through the arcade, though as a district to wander rather than one pinned address.

items.name: Mandarake Sapporo
items.why: Comics/toys/CDs/games/cosplay/dolls, duty-free over ¥5,000. Reviews call it genuinely good — one describes the whole NORBESA floor as "a whole floor of nerd shit."
items.crowd_tip: Honest caveat: specific trending categories (current Pokémon cards, hot anime figures) run shallower than a flagship store; go for breadth, not depth on any one franchise.

items.name: C-pla
items.how: Inside the Tanukikoji covered shopping arcade.
items.why: Opened Oct 2023, one of Hokkaido's largest capsule-toy shops — Sapporo's gacha landmark, new enough that it's easy for older sources to miss.

title: Sendai
intro: Honest gap, confirmed rather than assumed: Mandarake has no branch anywhere in Sendai or Tohoku — checked directly against Mandarake's own store list, which runs Tokyo (×4), Utsunomiya, Nagoya, Osaka, Kyoto, Fukuoka, Kokura, and Sapporo, with nothing in between.

items.name: Animate Sendai
items.how: 3 min from Sendai Station West Exit.
items.crowd_tip: One lead describes it as "actually small considering it's the city's only shop" and notes weekend crowding — useful for setting realistic expectations.

items.name: e-Beans
items.why: The same multi-floor building housing Animate — described by one enthusiast source as "Sendai's version of Nakano Broadway," with bookstores and dedicated anime-goods specialty shops beyond just the Animate tenant.

items.name: Seagull, Yamato-cho branch
items.why: A Tohoku-regional used-game chain that gets a reasonable notice ("pretty good selection of retro games, systems, accessories") for used games specifically.

items.name: Kikuya
items.why: A manga bookstore with DVD/CD/merch and manga-artist memorabilia — a further option beyond Animate.

title: Shipping it all home
body: Boxed figures, sealed games, and trading cards all qualify for the {{fact:entry-documents-5-000}}/store/day tax-free threshold (see the Plan tab for the Nov 1 system change that lands mid-trip). For anything too bulky or fragile to carry city-to-city, Yamato Ta-Q-Bin (see Transit) can forward a box straight to your final Sendai/Tokyo hotel instead of hauling it through three more flights. For larger hauls that won't fit in luggage at all, Mandarake ships internationally directly from any of its branches — worth asking about at checkout if a haul gets out of hand.
